Design revision: 7.1

$comment_entryClampMax: The rear socket's own position, so enemies never spawn past the player's last defense.
Uncapped repetition of the final step puts a 7-card hand past the end of the path: zero
engagement and a guaranteed full leak, which is an automatic loss for a legal, rare, and
genuinely impressive hand. Clamped, a 6-card hand keeps 3.0 engagement of 18.0.
Validated against max(geometry.socketPositions) - if the geometry moves, this must follow.

B.label: Soft escalation
B.note: Arm B. Expected to be the design if Arm C proves binary.

C.label: Hard escalation
C.note: Arm C. The curve the design documents specify.

cardPower.$comment: Sublinear in card value, approximately value^0.7. Key 10 covers all face cards; key 11 is an Ace held high.

$comment: Consecutive values in adjacent sockets. Direction-agnostic; Queen is wild; Ace matches its current state.
The 4-run tier (+35%) is absent on purpose, not by oversight: with three sockets per lane, no
cross-lane adjacency, and the junction excluded, a run of four is geometrically impossible.
It returns when socket counts grow - which is what makes the Surveyor relic a link tier rather
than a coverage bump. Validation requires exactly the reachable lengths 2..socketsPerLane, so
adding a socket will fail the load until this tier is restored.

enemies.$comment: Dealer face-card units. Stats are first-pass; the handoff provides qualitative descriptions only.

$comment_resolver_block: EVERYTHING FROM HERE TO 'rules' IS NOT SPECIFIED BY THE DESIGN.
The handoff specifies the enemy side of combat completely and the tower side not at all: there is
no fire rate, no meaning for 'power' in combat units, no tick rate, no splash or slow magnitude,
no junction penalty, no spawn schedule, and no base wave composition outside one paragraph of prose
in design/example-wave.md. The resolver cannot run without them.
These were decided deliberately rather than invented at a call site. Each is listed with its
reasoning in reference/tuning-constants.md section 'Invented for the resolver'.
They are first-pass and expected to be wrong, like every other number in this file.

$comment: ARCHITECTURE.md requires fixed simulation ticks and names 'rounding' as part of the forecast
contract, but specifies neither. 20 Hz gives 240-400 ticks over the 12-20 s wave window, and
every spacing value below lands on an exact tick boundary, so no spawn time needs rounding.
Positions, health, and damage stay double; nothing is rounded anywhere in the resolver.
Card power is damage per shot: shot = basePower * formationMultiplier * (1 + runBonus).
One shared cooldown rather than per-family cooldowns - the resolver contract names 'cooldown'
so it must exist, and a single value keeps this first pass honest about being invented.
The junction fires into both lanes at half damage; face cards are exempt per design/04.
junctionPathPosition is validated against the middle socket, not chosen independently of it.
design/04-cards-as-defenses.md gives the keywords 'splash' and 'slow' and no magnitudes.
Splash radius is a third of socket spacing, so it rewards hitting a clustered swarm without
reaching from one socket's kill zone into another's. Slow refreshes rather than stacks, so a
second Spade cannot compound into a hard stop.
design/05-battlefield.md names three orders and parameterises none of them. Hold takes a socket
position (per-tower board state, not tuned). Focus is an enum (per-tower). Only trigger-on-group
needs tuned numbers. An unset order is a no-op: an unordered tower uses the default target rule.
Per-type spacing exists on the enemy rows; nothing says when groups start or how they interleave.
Groups run sequentially within a lane - base wave, then Vanguard, then Dealer draws in draw order -
each at its own spacing, separated by groupGapSeconds. This gives a wave a readable shape and lands
in the 12-20 s window in combat.waveResolutionSeconds*.
dealerCardDeploysFullPack: a Dealer card deploys the whole pack from its enemy row (a 3 deploys 8
swarm, a King deploys 1 siege), which is what 'Swarm pack - many, fragile' against 'Siege engine'
describes. The Vanguard spawns at t=0 at the current entry point; 'already standing on the field'
is presentation, not a separate movement rule.
design/example-wave.md is the Milestone 3 acceptance test, so its setup ships as data.
Lane one: Bastion stakes, three armored soldiers (leak 2 each = 6 undefended).
Lane two: Vault stakes, a fast reinforcement package the doc says forecasts 6 damage undefended.
Fast raiders leak 1 each, so the package is SIX raiders, not the roster's five - encounter groups
carry explicit counts and override the roster default. The roster count stays the Dealer pack size.

$comment_overload: The busting card is destroyed and never placed, so there is no placement to inherit a lane from.
Targeting the highest current Visible Threat is deterministic, needs no declaration click during
the draw, and is unsteerable - the player cannot angle a bust into the lane they wanted.
